scope: Provisional ingredient-based screening only, never a complete classification for these health classes
warnings: A negative automatic result means only that this limited ingredient pathway did not establish a classification.
HPR 2(3)-(5) Schedule 4 prescribed classifications must be checked.
HPR 2.4 synergy, 2.5 classification at lower limits, 2.6 maximum concentration and 2.9 biological availability may alter results.
Use actual percentage concentration basis; gas ingredients require volume percent rather than mass-percent substitution.
Whole-mixture scientific evidence and valid bridging can change ingredient-based conclusions. The user may flag this to withhold automated candidates.

rules.concentrationMethod: Solid/liquid %w/w; gas %v/v with separately entered volume concentration.
rules.logic: Assess respiratory and skin branches independently. Category 1B only if no respiratory Category 1A ingredient at or above 0.1%.
Category 1B requires absence of Category 1A ingredient at or above 0.1%.

rules.priority: Category 1A > Category 1B > Category 2, subject to exceptions and conclusive whole-mixture evidence.
rules.nuance: HPR contains exceptions for whole-mixture conclusive positive and scientifically valid negative in-vivo germ cell mutagenicity tests. Generic ingredient Category 1 without A/B subcategory is flagged.
HPR whole-mixture conclusive positive and scientifically valid negative studies take precedence in specified exceptions.
Effects on or via lactation are a separate classification and can coexist with 1A/1B/2 under 8.7.5(2). Other conclusive mixture study exceptions and 8.7.6 bridging require review.

thresholds.exception: Lower documented concentration known to elicit the Category 3 effect may be used.

combinedCategory3.mayCoexistWith1Or2: Only Category 3 established by paragraph 8.8.5(1)(c) may be retained alongside 1/2 under (2).

rules.nuance: No summation of transient narcotic-effect and respiratory-irritation percentages across different endpoints.
Per-ingredient threshold only; do not invent additive sum for subthreshold ingredients.

conditions: Sum Cat1 aspiration ingredients each present ≥1% reaches 10%
Evaluate each layer's ingredient concentration and viscosity at 40°C independently per HPR 8.10.5(b)

rules.bridgingNuance: HPR 8.10.4 does not permit applying subsection 2.3(3) dilution when aspiration toxicant concentration <10%.

precedence.sensitisation: HPR 8.4.3 whole-mixture, 8.4.4 bridging, then 8.4.5 ingredients (independent respiratory/skin).
precedence.cmr: HPR 8.5-8.7 evaluate ingredient triggers first, subject to conclusive valid mixture-study exceptions and restricted bridging provisions.
precedence.stot: HPR 8.8.3 / 8.9.3 whole-mixture, 8.8.4 / 8.9.4 bridging, then 8.8.5 / 8.9.5 ingredient method.
precedence.aspiration: HPR 8.10.3 whole-mixture, 8.10.4 bridging, then 8.10.5 ingredient method.

notAutomated: All substantive whole-mixture scientific assessments and bridging decisions in these sections
HPR 2.5/2.6 evidence-based concentration deviations and 2.9 bioavailability
HPR 8.4 biologic assay interpretation and dose response
HPR 8.8/8.9 target organ and route-specific scientific evaluation
Bilingual labels, SDSs and conditional HPR Schedule 5 information elements
